dek: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor trailed PhilthyPhil by 81.9 points after the early Sunday games and won by 3.1 on Monday night. Monday's Bengals-Commanders game flipped three results, the commissioner won for the first time since Week 5, and three teams are tied at 6-5 for the last two playoff seats.

stories.h: Murrdawgs come back from 81.9 down, and PhilthyPhil blows a big lead for the second straight week
stories.body: After the early Sunday games PhilthyPhil led Murrdawgs Massage Parlor 102.3 to 20.4. Phil's lineup finished in the late window at 115.2 and then sat there. Murrdawgs still had four guys. Mike Evans (24.9) and George Kittle (18.4) cut the gap to 34.3 on Sunday night, and Joe Burrow (28.9) and Stefon Diggs (8.5) finished it on Monday: 118.3 to 115.2. A week ago Phil led PerryCock by 68.65 and lost. This time the hole was 81.9. Phil's best lineup was 128.2, which wins, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (15.7) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (7.7) on the bench, though Sleeper liked both starters ahead of them. Murrdawgs are 8-3, first in the standings, and their bye odds jumped from 65% to 85%. Phil is 7-4 with two straight losses, and the bye odds fell from 60% to 50%.

stories.h: Three teams at 6-5, two seats left, and the team on a three-game streak is on the outside
stories.body: The top four are set for now: Murrdawgs and Bad Bunny's Bush at 8-3, PhilthyPhil and Bijan al Gaib at 7-4. Behind them PerryCock, CeeDeez Nutz and Geno-Cide Smith are all 6-5 and two of them get in. PerryCock has won four straight and sits at 89%, which makes sense for a team second in points with 1,629.9 and a 76-34 all-play record. It is 6-5 only because it has allowed 1,521.95 points, the most in the league. CeeDeez Nutz jumped from 37% to 63% and took sixth. Geno-Cide Smith won its third straight and dropped from sixth to seventh anyway, because CeeDeez has 10.8 more points. Willy's odds went from 25% to 27%. Cheesehead10 fell to 5-6 and 15%, degr to 4-7 and 9%, and Open for Business is at 0%. Three weeks left.

stories.h: Six of the eight best bench scores were quarterbacks
stories.body: The highest bench score of the week was Dak Prescott's 49.15 for Geno-Cide Smith. Last week it was Dak Prescott's 49.85 for Geno-Cide Smith. That's 99.0 points of bench quarterback in two weeks, and Willy made the right call both times, because Patrick Mahomes scored 36.2 this week on a 30.8 projection. CeeDeez Nutz left Cam Ward on the bench again and he scored 28.7, after 25.45 on the bench last week. Bijan al Gaib sat Justin Herbert (27.75) behind Trevor Lawrence (19.75). PerryCock sat Bryce Young (22.5) behind Bo Nix (15.75), a week after starting Young for 10.1. PhilthyPhil had Caleb Williams (20.15) on the bench and Murrdawgs had Tyler Shough (18.5). Half this league has two quarterbacks and a coin to flip every Sunday.

stories.h: The $400 lead shrinks to 112.35 with three weeks left
stories.body: Murrdawgs scored 118.3 and PerryCock scored 137.95, so the points race got 19.65 closer. Murrdawgs have 1,742.25 and PerryCock 1,629.9. PhilthyPhil is 180.2 back, Bijan al Gaib 194.1 and Bad Bunny's Bush 197.45. Three regular-season weeks are left. PerryCock would need to outscore Connorj22 by about 37.5 a week to catch him, which it did by 19.65 this week. Possible. Not likely.

stories.h: The commissioner wins one, and the 1.01 doesn't care
stories.body: Matty Ice beat degr 105.55 to 100.35, ending a five-game losing streak and getting to 2-9. It was Matt's first win since beating PerryCock in Week 5. It cost nothing: non-playoff teams draft by reverse Maximum Points For, and Matty Ice's 979.7 is 360.1 below anyone else, so the 1.01 is still Matt's in every simulation. Matt also owns PhilthyPhil's and PerryCock's 2027 firsts. Phil lost, which helps. PerryCock won for the fourth straight time, which doesn't. The race for 1.02 got wider. Open for Business sits at 1,339.8 Max PF and ChrisUMD23 at 1,410.7, a gap of 70.9 that was 39.5 a week ago. Both lost again: five straight for Open for Business, four for ChrisUMD23. Open for Business's first belongs to Cheesehead10 and projects at an average slot of 2.14. ChrisUMD23's belongs to Murrdawgs at 3.61.

stories.h: The trade box score: McConkey and Washington call it a draw
stories.body: Ladd McConkey scored 20.7 for Cheesehead10 and Parker Washington scored 20.3 for Bijan al Gaib, after being swapped for each other in Week 5, and both teams lost. Ollie Gordon II scored 8.7 on an 11.4 projection in his first game for PhilthyPhil, in a 3.1-point loss. Derrick Henry scored 19.1 for ChrisUMD23 in a loss, and the team that sold him to Chris for a 2029 first is in first place. Tony Pollard, bought from Chris in Week 6, added 13.0 for Murrdawgs. Luther Burden III, who cost Chris a first and a second in Week 6, scored 3.3 on a 15.1 projection. Jared Goff, bought from Cheesehead10 in Week 5, scored 27.15 for Chris. And Tetairoa McMillan scored 19.1 in the commissioner's win, which is the most fun anyone has had with that trade from Matt's side.

t: C.J. Stroud scored 28.4 on Thursday night in Houston's 26-3 win over Indianapolis, and PhilthyPhil led before Murrdawgs had a player on the field. The early Sunday window made it a rout: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 27.8 and Bucky Irving 19.0, and Phil led 102.3 to 20.4. Murrdawgs' late window was worse than nothing. Cam Skattebo scored 5.8 on a 16.4 projection, Garrett Wilson 6.9 on 15.7 and Isaiah Likely 4.5 on 14.6. Phil's lineup was done after the late games at 115.2, up 77.6.

Then it got strange. San Francisco beat Minnesota 35-10 on Sunday night, and Mike Evans (24.9) and George Kittle (18.4) cut the lead to 34.3. On Monday Murrdawgs needed 34.4 from Joe Burrow and Stefon Diggs. Burrow scored 28.9, 6.4 under his projection, and Diggs scored 8.5. That's 37.4. Final: 118.3 to 115.2.

Phil can blame the bench a little. Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored 15.7 behind Bhayshul Tuten (8.3) and Deebo Samuel Sr. scored 7.7 behind Ryan Flournoy (2.1). Sleeper liked Tuten by 7.8 and Flournoy by 1.0, so both calls were defensible. The best lineup was 128.2, which wins by 9.9. Last week Phil's whole team played in the early window and lost a 68.65-point lead. This week it finished one window later and lost an 81.9-point lead. Next week, maybe schedule a guy for Monday.
Murrdawgs are 8-3, first, with bye odds up from 65% to 85% and title odds at 34%. Phil is 7-4 with two straight losses and bye odds down from 60% to 50%.
games.v: PhilthyPhil led by 81.9 and lost. The games keep going after lunch, Phil. They also keep going after dinner.

games.h: Bad Bunny's Bush Holds Off Three Commanders on Monday Night
t: Bad Bunny's Bush led this game after every window and still had to sweat Monday night. Jonathan Taylor gave them 6.7 on Thursday on a 14.4 projection, then Khalil Shakir (17.3), Chimere Dike (13.3) and D'Andre Swift (11.9) built a 32.8-point lead in the early games. Cheesehead10 got Ladd McConkey's 20.7 in the late window and went into Monday down 21.5.

Cheesehead10 had three Commanders left: Jayden Daniels, Rachaad White and Chig Okonkwo. Daniels scored 19.95 and Okonkwo 10.6. White, projected for 8.6, scored 0.0. Bad Bunny's got 12.3 from Tee Higgins, and the final was 104.2 to 100.95. A margin of 3.25 with a running back who scored nothing in the lineup.

The other running back slot belonged to Will Shipley, added off waivers this week for $0, who scored 0.9. Josh Cameron scored 7.4 on the bench behind Emeka Egbuka's 3.8, though Sleeper had Egbuka projected 10.2 to 3.7. Cheesehead10's best lineup was 104.55, which wins by 0.35. Bad Bunny's had its own problems: Josh Allen scored 19.2 on a 29.5 projection and Jaylen Warren scored 4.9 on 15.8, the second straight week Warren came in well under.

Bad Bunny's Bush snaps a two-game losing streak, moves to 8-3 and second, and its bye odds went from 38% to 45%. Cheesehead10 is 5-6 and eighth, and its playoff odds were cut in half, from 29% to 15%.
games.v: Bad Bunny's Bush led wire to wire. Cheesehead10 lost by 3.25 with a 0.0 and a 0.9 at running back.

games.h: CeeDee Lamb Shows Up for His Namesake, Antonio Williams Wins It Monday
t: CeeDeez Nutz got 32.2 from CeeDee Lamb in Dallas's 51-30 win over Tennessee, which is the least a man can do for the team named after him. Chuba Hubbard added 28.0 in Carolina's 35-33 win over Baltimore and Aaron Rodgers 20.25, and CeeDeez led 112.85 to 87.7 after the early games. Bijan al Gaib had Javonte Williams (24.1) and George Pickens (25.8) in the same Cowboys blowout and still trailed by 25.15.

Bijan came back in the late window. Parker Washington scored 20.3 and Trevor Lawrence 19.75 in Jacksonville's 23-18 loss to the Giants, and Bijan led by 0.4 going into Monday night. Courtland Sutton did not help. Denver scored 38 points and Sutton scored 0.0 on an 8.0 projection. On Monday, Antonio Williams scored 23.2 for CeeDeez on an 8.3 projection, Chase Brown scored 8.6 for Bijan on a 15.0 projection, and the final was 155.05 to 140.85, the high score of the week.

Both teams left a quarterback on the bench. CeeDeez sat Cam Ward (28.7) behind Rodgers (20.25), with Sleeper at 22.3 to 21.6 for Rodgers. Bijan sat Justin Herbert (27.75) behind Lawrence (19.75), with Sleeper at 25.8 to 21.7 for Lawrence. Bijan left 27.0 on the bench, and its best lineup, 167.85, would have won. Ty Johnson, the running back CeeDeez added for Kyler Murray last week, scored 12.7.

CeeDeez Nutz is 6-5, sixth, and its playoff odds went from 37% to 63%. Bijan al Gaib's four-game winning streak is over, and its bye odds fell from 35% to 15%. NotGomes, who owns Bijan's 2027 first, enjoyed this one.
games.v: CeeDeez Nutz trailed by 0.4 going into Monday and won by 14.2. Courtland Sutton's 0.0 was the difference, plus some.

games.h: PerryCock Spots ChrisUMD23 33.05 and Wins on Sunday Night
t: ChrisUMD23 played a nice game for three windows. David Montgomery, who scored 0.0 last week, scored 17.4 on Thursday night. Jared Goff (27.15), Emmett Johnson (26.3) and Derrick Henry (19.1) made it 106.75 to 73.7 after the early games. Chris's whole lineup was done after the late window, at 128.85, with a 26.9-point lead.

PerryCock still had three guys. Christian McCaffrey (14.2) and Justin Jefferson (13.7) played against each other in San Francisco's 35-10 win over Minnesota and turned the deficit into a 1.0-point lead. Ja'Marr Chase added 8.1 on Monday night on a 22.1 projection, the biggest miss of the week, and it was still enough. Final: 137.95 to 128.85. Travis Kelce scored 25.4 on a 13.0 projection and Chris Olave 21.2.

PerryCock benched Bryce Young a week after starting him for 10.1, and this week Young scored 22.5 on the bench while Bo Nix scored 15.75. Sleeper had Young ahead by 0.9. Justice Hill added 17.6 on the bench. PerryCock left 16.25 on the bench and won anyway. Chris's best lineup was 147.55, which wins, but the extra points came from Rashod Bateman (14.7) and Xavier Worthy (11.8), projected at 5.3 and 6.8. Nobody was starting them over Luther Burden III, who was projected for 15.1 and scored 3.3.
PerryCock has won four straight, is 6-5 and fifth, and its playoff odds went from 81% to 89%. ChrisUMD23 has lost four straight and is 3-8.
games.v: ChrisUMD23 led by 33.05 and ran out of players. PerryCock won with its quarterback and its best wide receiver both stinking.

games.h: Five Windows, Four Lead Changes, and a Commissioner Win
t: This was the most back-and-forth game of the week, and nobody outside these two teams watched it. Emari Demercado gave Matty Ice a 4.9-point lead on Thursday. degr went ahead by 10.2 after the early games behind 14.6 from Devaughn Vele, while Tetairoa McMillan's 19.1 in Carolina's 35-33 win kept Matt close. Then Fernando Mendoza scored 31.55 on a 15.0 projection and Malik Nabers added 18.5 in the late window, and Matt led by 22.25.

Brock Purdy took it back on Sunday night with 30.75 in San Francisco's 35-10 win, and degr led by 8.5. Matty Ice had one man left, Samaje Perine on Monday night. Perine scored 13.7 on a 7.8 projection. Final: 105.55 to 100.35.

The good news for the commissioner: no starter scored zero and nobody started from injured reserve, an improvement on the last two weeks. The bad news: Jack Bech scored 22.8 on the bench, playing for the same Raiders as Mendoza, while Jordyn Tyson scored 2.0 on a 10.7 projection and Demercado scored 4.9. Bech was projected for 5.4, so the lineup made sense on paper. Matt left 27.4 on the bench, second most in the league. degr left 0.9. Its best lineup was 101.25 and still loses. Ashton Jeanty's 27.9 on a 12.7 projection was wasted, and so were Kyle Monangai (1.8) and Makai Lemon (1.3).
Matty Ice is 2-9 and ended a five-game losing streak. degr is 4-7, its two-game winning streak is over, and its playoff odds fell from 25% to 9%. Losing to the commissioner hurts in December.
games.v: degr lost to Matty Ice with an almost perfect lineup. Matt won with a 2.0 from a starting receiver and a 22.8 on the bench.

games.h: Geno-Cide Smith Leads All Day, and Dak Prescott Scores 49 on the Bench Again
t: This one was over early. Geno-Cide Smith had three Texans on Thursday night, and Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Dalton Schultz combined for 22.6 in Houston's 26-3 win. Patrick Mahomes scored 36.2 in Kansas City's 34-7 win over Arizona, and Geno-Cide Smith led 98.8 to 31.1 after the early games. Jonah Coleman scored 36.9 for Open for Business in Denver's 38-24 win over the Raiders, the top score by any starter this week, and it cut the lead to 20.5. That was as close as it got. Final: 110.1 to 88.05.

Dak Prescott scored 49.15 on Willy's bench, a week after scoring 49.85 on Willy's bench. Sleeper had Mahomes up 30.8 to 26.8 and Mahomes scored 36.2, so it was the right call again. Willy's best lineup was 134.45.

Open for Business got 9.75 from Kirk Cousins on a 21.5 projection, 0.0 from Ja'Kobi Lane on a 6.4 projection, and 3.2 from Tyler Warren. Ted Hurst III scored 22.6 on the bench on a 1.8 projection. A best lineup of 116.15 would have won, and nobody was starting Ted Hurst III.
Geno-Cide Smith has won three straight and is 6-5, but dropped to seventh on points, with playoff odds of 27%. Open for Business has lost five straight, is 4-7, and its playoff odds hit 0%.
games.v: Geno-Cide Smith led wire to wire. Not much drama, unless you count 49.15 points on the bench.

awards.p: The top score by any starter, 19.4 over his projection, in a 22.05-point loss. Open for Business has lost five straight.

Projected for 22.1, scored 8.1, the biggest miss of the week. PerryCock won by 9.1 anyway.
The best total of the week, with 32.2 from CeeDee Lamb himself and 23.2 on Monday night from Antonio Williams.
Projected for 8.3. CeeDeez trailed by 0.4 when he took the field and won by 14.2.
Projected for 8.6, scored 0.0 on Monday night. Cheesehead10 lost by 3.25.

awards.who: Bryce Young · PerryCock · 22.5 on the bench
awards.p: Started last week and scored 10.1. Benched this week and scored 22.5, while Bo Nix scored 15.75.
Projected for 15.0, scored 31.55, and gave the commissioner a 22.25-point lead in a game he won by 5.2.
Phil's lineup was finished after the late Sunday games, up 77.6. Murrdawgs had four players left and needed all of them.

note: Thursday's Colts-Texans game gave PhilthyPhil a 28.4-point head start, ChrisUMD23 a 17.4-point lead and Geno-Cide Smith 22.6 points of Texans. The early Sunday window, led by Dallas's 51-30 win over Tennessee and Carolina's 35-33 win over Baltimore, built big leads for Phil, Chris, Geno-Cide Smith and CeeDeez Nutz. The late window, with Denver's 38-24 win over the Raiders, put Matty Ice ahead of degr and Bijan al Gaib ahead of CeeDeez Nutz by 0.4. San Francisco's 35-10 win over Minnesota on Sunday night flipped PerryCock past ChrisUMD23 and degr past Matty Ice. Then Washington's 22-20 win over Cincinnati on Monday flipped three games: Murrdawgs over Phil, CeeDeez Nutz over Bijan al Gaib, and Matty Ice over degr.
